mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand with nascent housing recovery, which depresses cyclical sectors and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least one confirmed recession window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that pressures firms' cost structures, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during any period of confirmed late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by > 1.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during a confirmed manufacturing recession.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate by more than 0.75 percentage points within a single month signals an emergency monetary easing, which boosts risk appetite and yields positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during any emergency easing period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals robust household demand, which supports corporate earnings and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during any confirmed expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals a significant labor market weakening, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during any confirmed labor market downturn.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during any confirmed housing recovery.
